about.title: Moreno Valley Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails in Moreno Valley can hurt someone anywhere in the city: a space heater in a home near Perris Boulevard, a power tool on a job site off Alessandro Boulevard, a tire that separates at freeway speed on SR-60. Moreno Valley is home to roughly 204,000 people in Riverside County, and the everyday goods they rely on are supposed to be safe when used as intended. When one isn't, California law treats the situation differently from an ordinary accident. Under strict liability, you generally don't have to prove the maker was careless. You need to show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the manufacturer, the distributor, and the store that sold it. The most important step is often the simplest: keep the product. Don't repair it, return it, or throw it out. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Moreno Valley Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You don't have to prove carelessness
items.desc: California product cases often rest on strict liability, so the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused your injury, not on the manufacturer's state of mind. Attorneys in our network know how to build a claim around that standard.

items.title: Every link in the chain can be examined
items.desc: The company that designed the product, the one that built it, the distributor, and the Moreno Valley retailer that sold it may each share responsibility. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Help protecting the evidence early
items.desc: The product itself is usually the heart of the case, and it's easy to lose through a return, a repair, or a well-meaning cleanup. Connecting quickly means someone can advise you on preserving it before it disappears.

items.question: I was in a crash on SR-60 in Moreno Valley and I think a part on my car failed. Is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be. Moreno Valley recorded 842 injury collisions in 2025, and in some of those, a tire, airbag, brake, or seatbelt may not have performed as designed. If a defect contributed to your injuries, the manufacturer and others in the supply chain may be responsible in addition to any driver at fault. Keep the vehicle and the part from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has looked at it.

items.question: Do I have to show the company was negligent?
items.answer: Usually not. California applies strict liability to many product claims, which means you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company meant well or followed its own procedures is often beside the point.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Hold onto it, along with any packaging, manuals, and receipts, and photograph it as it is now. Don't send it back to the store or the maker, even if they ask, and don't try to fix it. The product is the central piece of evidence, and an independent attorney can arrange for it to be examined properly.
